questions.q: (R)-Butan-2-ol is treated with SOCl₂ in the absence of base. The product is:
questions.explain: Without base the chlorosulfite collapses as a tight ion pair and chlorine is delivered to the front face (SNi), so configuration is retained.

questions.q: The same alcohol, (R)-butan-2-ol, is treated with SOCl₂ in pyridine. The mechanism and product are:
questions.explain: Pyridine forms a pyridinium salt and frees Cl⁻, which attacks the back side in an SN2 step (Darzens process), giving inversion.

questions.q: Which reagent converts a chiral secondary alcohol into the alkyl chloride with inversion of configuration?
questions.explain: PCl₃ forms an O–P intermediate that chloride displaces by backside attack (SN2); SOCl₂ alone and PCl₅ without base are treated as SNi (retention).

questions.q: Why is SOCl₂ preferred for converting alcohols into alkyl chlorides?
options: It works without forming any intermediate
Both by-products, SO₂ and HCl, are gases, so the alkyl chloride is obtained pure
questions.explain: The gaseous by-products escape, leaving the alkyl halide free of contaminants; the reaction goes through an alkyl chlorosulfite intermediate.
